frontPage.headline: 18th BRICS Summit Concludes in New Delhi: Key Outcomes on Trade, Governance, and Security
frontPage.summary: The 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi resulted in the adoption of the New Delhi Declaration, emphasizing United Nations Security Council (UNSC) reforms, enhanced Global South representation, and joint counter-terrorism efforts. Member nations pushed for local currency trade settlement mechanisms while opposing unilateral trade barriers and protectionist carbon tariffs.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Crucial for GS-II International Relations syllabus covering multilateral forums, reform of global institutions, and India's leadership role in representing the Global South.

frontPage.headline: India-China Bilateral Dialogue Emphasizes Border Peace as Precondition for Normalization
frontPage.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping acknowledged ongoing progress in bilateral relations during their meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. India reiterated that maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) remains essential for sustainable diplomatic and economic ties.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Directly impacts GS-II India's bilateral relations and neighborhood policy, highlighting the balance between economic engagements and border security management.

frontPage.headline: Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) Operationalization Boosts National Logistics Network
frontPage.summary: The full operationalization of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor marks a major milestone in completing India's 2,843-km dedicated freight network. The corridor aims to drastically cut transit time, lower logistics costs as a percentage of GDP, and decongest the conventional railway network.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Relevant for GS-III Infrastructure and Economy, specifically in reducing supply chain costs and achieving targets set under the National Logistics Policy.

frontPage.headline: BRICS Nations Reject Unilateral Green Trade Barriers Including EU's Carbon Border Tax
frontPage.summary: BRICS member countries collectively voiced opposition to unilateral protectionist trade measures introduced under the pretext of environmental policies, explicitly citing mechanisms like the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). The bloc argued that such taxes violate WTO principles and disproportionately penalize developing economies.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Intersects GS-II International Trade and GS-III Environment & Climate Change negotiations, focusing on common but differentiated responsibilities (CBDR) and non-tariff barriers.

frontPage.headline: Study Links 70% of North India's Winter Air Pollution Variability to Western Disturbances
frontPage.summary: A new atmospheric study reveals that up to 70% of the year-to-year variation in winter air pollution levels across northern India is dictated by the frequency and intensity of Western Disturbances. Years with more frequent western disturbances witness better pollutant dispersion due to associated rainfall and wind patterns.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Connects GS-I Geography (meteorological phenomena like Western Disturbances) with GS-III Pollution and Environmental Degradation.

frontPage.headline: Supreme Court Directs FSSAI on Front-of-Pack Warning Labels and School Nutritional Literacy
frontPage.topic: Issues Relating to Health & Social Sector Governance
frontPage.summary: The Supreme Court has asked the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) for a clear timeline to implement mandatory Front-of-Pack Labeling (FOPL) for processed foods high in sugar, salt, and fats. The apex court also advised integrating nutritional literacy into school curricula to shield vulnerable children from unhealthy dietary choices.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Important for GS-II Public Health, Regulatory Frameworks, and Judicial Interventions in Social Welfare.

gs1.headline: Mitochondrial Study Links Kerala's Malabari Goat Genetics to Historical Indian Ocean Spice Route
gs1.summary: Researchers analyzing the complete mitochondrial genome of the indigenous Malabari goat found genetic markers indicating historical gene flow along the maritime Spice Route of the Indian Ocean, providing biological corroboration for ancient trade links between the Malabar coast and West Asia.
gs1.whyItMatters: Provides multi-disciplinary evidence (genomics aiding history) regarding India's ancient maritime trade networks across the Indian Ocean.

gs2.headline: Government Employees Resigning to Fight Elections Cannot Demand Reinstatement, Rules Rajasthan High Court
gs2.topic: Role of Civil Services in a Democracy & Neutrality
gs2.summary: The Rajasthan High Court affirmed that a civil servant who resigns from service to contest elections on a political party ticket cannot later seek reinstatement into public service if defeated. The court reiterated that active political participation compromises the core constitutional requirement of civil service political neutrality.
gs2.whyItMatters: Highly relevant for GS-II (Civil Services) and GS-IV (Ethics in Governance), reinforcing conduct rules and political non-partisanship among public servants.

gs2.headline: BRICS Summit Focuses on Local Currency Settlement Systems Over Common Currency
gs2.summary: Clarifying its stand during the BRICS discussions on financial track integration, India ruled out creating a unified BRICS supranational currency. Instead, member states agreed to focus on interlinking national fast-payment systems and promoting cross-border trade settlements using local currencies to lower transaction costs.
gs2.whyItMatters: Crucial for understanding India's calibrated foreign policy on de-dollarisation and maintaining balance between BRICS commitments and global financial architectures.

gs3.headline: RBI Rejects Tata Sons' De-registration Bid, Mandates Compliance with Upper-Layer NBFC Listing Norms
gs3.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) turned down a request by Tata Sons to surrender its Core Investment Company (CIC) registration. As an Upper-Layer NBFC (NBFC-UL) under the RBI's scale-based regulatory framework, Tata Sons remains legally bound to list its shares publicly.
gs3.whyItMatters: Demonstrates the RBI's strict adherence to scale-based regulation for systemically important non-banking financial entities to ensure corporate governance and financial stability.

gs3.headline: DRDO to Establish New Advanced Missile Testing Range in West Bengal
gs3.summary: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is setting up a secondary missile and weapon testing facility along the coastline of West Bengal to supplement the existing Integrated Test Range (ITR) at Chandipur and Abdul Kalam Island in Odisha.
gs3.whyItMatters: Enhances India's strategic defence testing capability and reduces operational load on existing east-coast testing sites.

quiz.question:
With reference to Core Investment Companies (CICs) in India, consider the following statements:
1. A CIC is an NBFC carrying on the business of acquisition of shares and securities.
2. It holds not less than 90% of its total assets in the form of investment in equity shares, preference shares, debt or loans in group companies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
quiz.explanation: Both statements are correct according to Reserve Bank of India regulations governing Core Investment Companies.

quiz.question: Recently discovered 'Gegeneophis chandgadi' belongs to which of the following animal groups?
quiz.explanation: Gegeneophis chandgadi is a newly discovered species of legless amphibian (caecilian) found in the Western Ghats.

quiz.question: Which of the following atmospheric phenomena accounts for a major share of the inter-annual variability of winter air pollution in Northern India?
quiz.explanation: Recent scientific research shows that approximately 70% of the year-to-year variation in winter air pollution across North India is driven by the frequency of Western Disturbances.

quiz.question: The term 'Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism' (CBAM), frequently seen in news, is associated with which international entity?
quiz.explanation: CBAM is a measure introduced by the European Union to place a fair price on the carbon emitted during the production of carbon-intensive goods imported into the EU.

quiz.question: Which of the following ports serves as the western terminus of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC)?
quiz.explanation: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor connects Dadri in Uttar Pradesh to Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) near Mumbai.

schemes.name: Dedicated Freight Corridor Project
schemes.beneficiaries: Industrial corridors, exporters, freight operators, and logistics service providers
schemes.objective: Construct dedicated high-speed heavy-haul rail tracks across major economic arteries to separate freight from passenger trains, lowering logistics costs.
keyFeatures: Covers Western DFC (Dadri to JNPT) and Eastern DFC (Ludhiana to Dankuni)
Automated train control and higher axle load capability
Direct integration with major sea ports along coastal routes
schemes.funding: Funded jointly by Ministry of Railways, World Bank, and JICA (Japan International Cooperation Agency)
schemes.upscRelevance: Crucial infrastructure project under GS-III related to economic growth, logistics speed, and reducing carbon intensity of transportation.
